topology: one Linux node, two independent JuiceFS FUSE clients, shared SQLite metadata and file object store; reference-only multi-client control, not a production topology
identity_mechanism: JuiceFS volume UUID plus cross-client inode and visibility probes
reference_hardware: Amp E2B orb; Linux 6.1.158 x86_64; local SQLite metadata and local file object store; exact CPU/memory are variable shared sandbox resources

identity_evidence.name: same_namespace_inode
identity_evidence.detail: cross-client probe resolves to the same filesystem object

identity_evidence.name: distinct_client_root_objects
identity_evidence.detail: aliasing one local root is not evidence of independent clients

identity_evidence.name: declared_independent_mounts
identity_evidence.detail: operator topology assertion; identity tests alone do not prove a shared backend

failure_injection.detail: With the recorded zero-metadata-cache mount options, killed client B during repeated 4 MiB write+fsync. The writer returned ENOTCONN after 3246391296 bytes were visible from client A, so the operation was classified outcome unknown and was not replayed. Remounted client B with the same options and revalidated cross-client visibility before rerunning the full suite.

recovery.name: full_revalidation_after_remount
